work_order.root_cause: The work order used the TEXT OF A DOC COMMENT as its acceptance criterion, and left four of its six criteria with no `verify` field, so the schema's default (browser) instructed QA to verify in the running app four claims that have no browser surface at all. .sdlc/bin/lib/qa-consistency.js:186 reads an absent `verify` as anything but 'test' and rejects a criterion QA proved by citing ci - which is the only honest proof available for a reading check. I ran that gate myself against the ledger work order and it rejects FIVE criteria (AC-2, AC-3, AC-4, AC-5, AC-6), not the single AC-6 the run log printed, because the log prints only the first error. Underneath the marking mistake is a rule the work order broke: an acceptance criterion is an observable claim about the product, not a description of the fix. AC-2's own text states the rule behaviourally ('the guarantee holds for every spend row that names a currency, and it names the one class of row for which it does not') and then failed to assert it behaviourally, asserting the comment instead - so no test and no browser could discharge it, and citing ci was the only move left. The same rule-break produced the three defects this PR actually shipped, all of them comments making claims nothing checks: (1) the new test comment at test/web/pages.test.js:1269 cites pages.js:881 and :897 for the two cards.map(experimentCard) sites, but the plan computed its line numbers against main and its own comment edits above them moved both sites by six lines, so on eae9a62 the sites are 887 and 903 and 881 is `if (state === 'partial') {`; (2) the rewritten comments in src/api/routes.js and src/web/pages.js now assert as durable fact that a spend row carrying NO currency is still summed and still draws a CPL, and nothing pins that - the existing leniency case (test/domain/measurement.test.js, the 'excludes foreign-currency spend rows' test) exercises a currency-less row only against a valid 'INR' tenant, and the ZZZ sweep fixture creates no spend rows at all; (3) found here and named by no prior review, the money() comment in src/web/pages.js cites the four cases that pin its 'INR' fallback by ORDINAL (15, 52, 53, 55), and an ordinal moves whenever a test is added above it - on main those same four tests are 17, 57, 58 and 60, so the shipped comment already misdirects a reader on the default branch. A comment that points at something that moved is the exact defect class issue #72 exists to remove, and this PR added three of them while removing others.
work_order.understanding: The previous work order's technical diagnosis was RIGHT and its acceptance contract was WRONG, and the second half is what sent this back twice. I re-verified the code claims line by line against eae9a62 rather than trusting them, and they all hold: the sweep is genuinely non-vacuous on /experiments, the three narrowed comments genuinely describe the code, and the implementation is correct - 64 pass / 0 fail in test/web/pages.test.js, and the caps mutation still reds 38, 45, 53, 56, 57 with the sweep among them. So no implementation work needs redoing and no root-cause diagnosis needs rewriting. WHAT WAS WRONG: the work order accepted on comment text. AC-2, AC-3 and AC-5 read as 'read the comment and confirm it says X' and AC-6 as a byte-identity check. This change edits comments and tests and moves no page, route or user-visible state, so none of the four has a browser surface. The plan gave AC-1 `verify: "test"` and left the other five unset, the schema default applied, QA - which cannot produce in-app proof for a comment and knows it - cited ci, and the gate refused, correctly. I ran the gate against the ledger work order and reproduced it exactly, and it is five criteria wide rather than the one the run log shows. I also reject the triage's proposed repair, which was to add `verify: "test"` to those criteria: it turns the gate green while leaving four criteria no test can discharge, which is a criterion laundered past the check rather than fixed. Restating each as the product claim it already names is cheap and marking them would not be, which is why the restatement is the fix. This is the 'criterion is what is wrong' case, and I can justify it without referring to the implementation at all: AC-2's own stated rule is behavioural, and the criterion asserted the comment rather than the rule. BEYOND THE MARKING: the failed run also left three real defects on the branch, all confirmed by reading the files. The stale file:line citation (test/web/pages.test.js names pages.js:881/897; the sites are 887/903 and 881 is a different statement) is a comment sending the next reader to the wrong line - the exact class this ticket exists to remove. The unpinned leniency is more load-bearing: the rewritten comments now promise in writing that a currency-less spend row is still summed and still draws a CPL, and I confirmed that is true end-to-end (live ingest, ZZZ tenant, spend_micros 5000000, a real CPL, a rupee tile on the dashboard) and that nothing pins it. A comment asserting a behaviour nothing checks is how the original overstatement happened, one release later. The third, which I found here, is the same class as the second: the money() comment names its four covering cases by ordinal, and those ordinals are already wrong on main. Two things I checked and found need NO work, which is why the file list is three test files and one comment rather than the previous revision's five: the routes.js and pages.js comments ALREADY name computeFunnel and normaliseGrowthEvent for the lines they cite, so the previous revision's proposed src edits were no-ops; and every restated criterion's underlying claim already holds in code. I answer the three plan-reviewer objections on the refused revision explicitly: the counts are recomputed as 66 / 308 / 48 and every one of them is pinned to its base commit alongside the four test names, so the number and the list cannot disagree in one sentence; the citation guard is specified ONE way - option (b), parsed citations, with the line number read out of the comment and never hardcoded, which is the version AC-8's own check text describes; and no acceptance criterion names a line number as its verification step, because the branch is three commits behind main and main's pages.js has the money() fallback at 354 and the two cards.map sites at 977/993. review.title: The new assertion extracts its subject with `page.match(/data-testid="caps">[^<]*/)[0]`. When the caps span is absent the regex returns null and `[0]` throws a TypeError before assert.equal ever runs, so the test fails with 'Cannot read properties of null (reading 0)' — an error naming neither the route, the branch, nor the expected string. The assertion message that would have diagnosed it is unreachable in exactly the case it was written for. The test does still fail (so this is not a vacuity defect), but a mutation that removes a branch now produces a message that reads like a harness bug rather than a currency regression.

review.title: The final paragraph of resolveTenantCurrency's doc comment is a six-line changelog narrating the relationship between issue #66, its QA run, PR #70 and issue #68, carrying two concrete figures (7_200_000_000 spend, a ₹2,400.00 tile) that describe a baseline this codebase DELIBERATELY REVERSED. That is the wrong kind of content for this comment and the wrong place for it. The rest of src/ uses issue references as one-clause provenance tags — `issue #22` at pages.js:472, repositories.js:559, routes.js:401, `issue #21` at db.js:164 — never as a narrative with numbers. The 3am test: a reader paged to resolveTenantCurrency who has not read issues #66 and #68 and PR #70 cannot use this paragraph, and the figures are actively hazardous to skim, because 'a ZZZ tenant reading 7_200_000_000 spend' reads as a statement about current behaviour when it is a statement about behaviour that was removed. The behaviour claim itself is correct — I checked it, and a bad code does read 0 spend and null CPL, since computeFunnel returns `qualified_cpl_micros: volume > 0 && spend > 0 ? ... : null` (src/domain/measurement.js:217) and spend is 0 when every currency-carrying row is skipped. It is only the placement and the stale numbers that are wrong. The work order's justification — that PR #70's description was the alternative and is closed — does not hold, because the durable record the paragraph claims to be is already git history, and the review trail is on the PR.
